items.summary: Version 2.0 preserves the original June 2026 Bridge Settlement manuscript and adds a separately dated October 2026 supplement. The addendum introduces Residual Strategic Optionality as an extension of Stakeholder Coherence Theory, examining the incentives of actors capable of disrupting negotiated settlements. It also compares the Bridge Settlement with Jeffrey Sachs's October 2026 peace framework for Ukraine, identifying areas of conceptual convergence and distinguishing the Bridge Settlement's emphasis on reciprocal economic interests, institutional participation, and self-reinforcing peace mechanisms. The original manuscript remains unchanged. This study develops a comparative Bayesian framework for evaluating natural zoonotic and research-associated hypotheses for the proximal origin of SARS-CoV-2 under incomplete evidence. To reduce double counting, correlated observations are consolidated into three causal blocks addressing phenotype and proximal adaptation, the Huanan Seafood Wholesale Market and early epidemic topology, and the Wuhan sarbecovirus research environment. The central calibration yields a likelihood ratio of approximately 1.49 favoring research-associated emergence, while alternative defensible calibrations reverse or strengthen that preference, demonstrating substantial sensitivity to evidentiary weighting. The paper introduces the “Missing Bridge” as the unresolved proximal viral population and transmission history connecting deeper sarbecovirus ancestry to sustained human transmission. It argues that provenance-rich evidence—including authenticated proximal viruses, earliest-human genomic and epidemiological linkage, and upstream ecological or research records—has substantially greater discriminatory value than additional circumstantial observations. The resulting assessment is characterized as  preference without closure .
items.title: The Missing Bridge

items.summary: Multibeam imaging sonar produces intensity images degraded by coherent speckle and system-induced blur, while clean reflectivity targets are rarely available. Existing despeckling methods often rely on simplified intensity-domain noise models, synthetic clean targets, or blind-spot self-supervision, and typically do not jointly model deblurring and speckle suppression. We propose a physics-consistent self-supervised framework for joint despeckling and deblurring of multibeam imaging sonar. A stochastic coherent image-formation model yields a conditional-mean forward operator that relates latent scene reflectivity to expected intensity through the squared magnitude of the system point spread function. We then use registered multi-frame sonar sequences to train without clean ground truth images, showing that, under an idealized inter-frame conditional-mean condition, the expected paired loss equals the corresponding forward-prediction loss up to a network-independent constant. To stabilize the ill-conditioned inverse problem, we further adapt robust equivariant imaging using stochastic coherent simulation and introduce a paired forward prediction error metric for ground-truth-free evaluation. Experiments on two real multibeam sonar datasets demonstrate a favourable balance between forward-prediction agreement, homogeneous-region speckle suppression, and preservation of visible structural boundaries compared with representative baselines.
items.title: Self-Supervised Multibeam Sonar Restoration via Coherent Forward Modeling

items.summary: Gratitude can concern a benefit received, a harm that did not occur, or the conditions that make one's own assumptions examinable. We develop the proposal that appreciating these conditions can orient practice toward realizing emptiness: examining how distinctions arise, relinquishing their assumed intrinsic necessity, and retaining their conditional usefulness. The argument distinguishes an observed absence, a missing observation, counterfactual valuation and non-reification, and places their differences in dialogue with explicitly situated philosophical and scriptural sources. We reconstruct Fisher, Sandved Smith and Hohwy's gratitude and gaze notebooks, then separate faithful reconstruction from corrected experiments and new mechanisms. GNN-declared paired recall experiments use 5120 independent agent-world units, matched environmental exposure and replay dose, normalized likelihoods, and independent predictive assessment. Pinned Realizing Emptiness interfaces supply structural admission and finite mathematical comparators. An enacted inquiry model separates appreciation, costly activity, access to alternatives and evidence-responsive retention or revision; explicit learning-to-gaze and joint scene/encoding experiments examine transfer and identifiability. Exact count enumeration, mathematical nulls, paired controls and joint bootstrap inference make the resulting software claims independently checkable. Selective positive recall reduces the declared optimism summary, while its predictive consequences depend on the world mixture and the specified transfer bridge. Counterfactual absence valuation preserves inference by construction. Accessible inquiry can revise a contradicted restriction and retain a useful one; activity without access instead incurs costs while preserving rigid forecasts. Exact analysis exposes rare adverse selections absent from seeded realizations. The original gaze code reproduces the pre-intervention occupancy but contains no implemented after intervention. Our active-scene extension finds a context-dependent access advantage without an additional inquiry-specific predictive advantage. Joint scene/encoding inquiry distinguishes learning an encoding from combining it with scene evidence: observationally equivalent labels remain unidentifiable, and excluded hypotheses cannot be recovered. Known-answer fixtures also retain skew-related undercoverage and unavailable rare-event estimates rather than treating replication size as a remedy for every inferential failure. The contribution is a reproducible account of enabling operations and their limits, together with a falsifiable human research program that separates inquiry value from patience, anticipated good news and instrumental information demand. Synthetic model results establish neither human gratitude nor contemplative realization or clinical benefit. Code, declared models and reproducibility materials are available at github.com/docxology/thanks_for_nothing .
items.title: Thanks for Nothing: Gratitude, Model Revisability, and the Practice of Realizing Emptiness

items.summary: Biological-Digital-Twin-Driven Microrobotic Sampling Decisions at the Limit STARLI Research Institute XXIX — Flagship Research Monograph 10 What if the next scientific sample could be selected not merely to collect more data, but to distinguish between competing explanations of biological behavior? Biological-Digital-Twin-Driven Microrobotic Sampling Decisions at the Limit explores a prospective research architecture combining versioned biological digital twins, active learning, microrobotic sampling, uncertainty quantification, and mechanistic model discrimination. The central question is whether a computational twin can identify safe, informative sampling actions that distinguish competing biological mechanisms more effectively than conventional experimental schedules, while retaining the ability to recognize model inadequacy and abstain from unsupported decisions. The proposed framework treats biological digital twins as revisable scientific models rather than exact replicas of living systems. Its reference environment is a controlled, nonclinical microfluidic platform containing two declared dynamical mechanisms and a third withheld mechanism reserved for evaluating open-world uncertainty and model failure. The research architecture is organized around five interconnected layers: versioned biological modeling, explicit prior assumptions and knowledge gaps, physically constrained predictive interrogation, comparative adaptive experimentation, and independent requalification. The manuscript develops thirty candidate mathematical research plates covering Bayesian mechanism inference, conditional information gain, experimental identifiability, observation uncertainty, transport dynamics, calibration, model discrepancy, and decision safety. These mathematical structures are connected to eighty-two research chapters, five independently paginated investigation sections per chapter, two hundred detailed Research Gates, and thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos. Each Research Gate is intended as a transferable research question that future investigators may test, challenge, refine, or reject. The proposed evaluation compares twin-guided sampling against optimized fixed schedules, established experimental-design approaches, and alternative active-learning policies under matched physical constraints and experimental budgets. Particular attention is given to blinded mechanism identification, probabilistic calibration, out-of-distribution rejection, specimen integrity, model-version accountability, and explicit stopping conditions. The volume includes DOI-linked methodological literature and a staged nonclinical verification pathway. Scientific status and limitations: This manuscript presents a conceptual methodological research program, not completed experimental validation. Its integrated hypotheses, mathematical proposals, and experimental architectures remain subject to independent technical review and empirical testing. The manuscript does not establish clinical efficacy, diagnostic reliability, therapeutic benefit, or proven superiority of microrobotic digital-twin systems. The work also acknowledges remaining editorial limitations, including recurring methodological language that requires further substantive review before the manuscript can be regarded as a fully refined scientific monograph. The broader purpose of this research is to develop scientific systems that can remain useful even when their initial models are incomplete. Rather than demanding certainty from a digital twin, the proposed framework asks whether future autonomous research tools can become more transparent, corrigible, experimentally accountable, and capable of recognizing the boundaries of their own knowledge. Within the STARLI research continuum, this volume is intended as an evolving research inheritance for future human and artificial-intelligence investigators. Language: English Research Type: Conceptual and Methodological Research Monograph Edition

items.summary: Diffusion large language models (dLLMs) enable flexible masked generation through bidirectional context modeling, but this capability also introduces a distinct jailbreak attack surface. We find that a harmful response to a given query naturally serves as an effective jailbreak template: simply masking a subset of its tokens can induce a dLLM to reconstruct harmful content. Based on this observation, we propose RMT-Jailbreak, a general framework that transfers existing autoregressive (AR) jailbreak attacks to dLLMs through their induced harmful responses. RMT-Jailbreak converts an AR-generated harmful response into a high-mask-ratio template using uniform token retention, and further applies prompt-based safety filtering to mask any remaining visible harmful content. The refined template is then provided to the target dLLM for bidirectional reconstruction. Extensive experiments across multiple AR jailbreak methods and target dLLMs demonstrate the effectiveness and generality of RMT-Jailbreak, revealing strong cross-paradigm transferability of jailbreak attacks.
items.title: Harmful Responses Are Jailbreak Templates: Transferring Autoregressive Jailbreaks to Diffusion Language Models

items.summary: L4 is a generic, reversible, linearly-typed, low-level language intended as an intermediate language for compiling reversible programming languages to reversible machines. L4 is intended to replace and generalise RSSA, a reversible SSA form. Inspiration is drawn from other low-level reversible languages such as HSSA. In this paper, we define L4 first informally, and then give a formal type system and a bidirectional small-step semantics for L4: The rules have direction indicators to determine forwards or backwards execution, and the direction can be changed during execution.
items.title: The Reversible Intermediate Language L4, its Type System, and its Bidirectional Small-Step Semantics

items.summary: We envision a general-purpose protein foundation model as a unified, interactive model of sequence, structure, and function, capable of understanding, generation, and cross-modal translation while retaining the instruction-following and reasoning capabilities of modern LLMs. Toward this vision, we introduce Trion-1, the first native, unified, multimodal diffusion language model (dLLM) for proteins. Trion-1 is built on two key design choices: (1) a unified discrete token space that jointly represents sequence, structure, and natural language; (2) a dLLM backbone that replaces strict left-to-right factorization with bidirectional or semi-bidirectional token interactions, enabling global residue communication and long-range contact modeling that are naturally suited to structure modeling. This formulation unifies six core capabilities: folding, inverse folding, sequence understanding, structure understanding, sequence design, and structure design, while retaining the native language capabilities of general-purpose LLMs. On established benchmarks, Trion-1 achieves broadly competitive performance. In folding, Trion-1 achieves a TM-score above 0.8 with a single sample under strict homology control, matching or exceeding the existing tri-modal model using 200 samples. For sequence understanding, Trion-1 performs on par with top-tier LLMs such as Claude Opus 4.7 (62.37%). These results support well-aligned sequence-structure-language representations and strong cross-modal generative capabilities.
items.title: Trion-1: Unifying Language, Protein Sequence, and Structure with Diffusion Language Models

items.summary: Overview This software package accompanies the study Resolvability of Ionospheric Currents From Multi-LEO Magnetometry . It provides computational tools for investigating how multi-altitude satellite magnetic observations constrain three-dimensional ionospheric currents. The package implements a divergence-free spherical Mie magnetic-field representation and a Bayesian inversion framework for evaluating magnetic-field and current reconstruction, degrees of freedom for signal (DFS), physical-current information, and posterior uncertainty. Main Features Spherical-harmonic Mie forward modeling and three-component current reconstruction. Bayesian inversion with full posterior covariance propagation. Resolution and recoverability diagnostics for different satellite configurations and observation altitudes. Physical-current information analysis and regularization-sensitivity experiments. Synthetic current-recovery experiments, calibration routines, and figure-generation workflows. Python and optional MATLAB implementations, with independent numerical verification. Sample Swarm-A/B orbital positions for geometry tests and a self-contained synthetic inversion example. What's New in This Version 3 This release provides a corrected scientific implementation and updated reproducibility tools. The principal corrections include: Correcting the colatitude derivative of the associated Legendre functions used in the spherical-harmonic operator. Restoring the radial magnetic-field contribution of the quadratic poloidal Mie term, ensuring consistency with the continuous divergence-free representation. Updating the corresponding current-reconstruction and recoverability calculations. Clarifying the scaled coefficient parameterization, Bayesian prior, and interpretation of coefficient-space resolution diagnostics. Improving numerical verification, reproducibility workflows, and documentation. The updated calculations continue to support the importance of satellite altitude separation for constraining specified ionospheric current structures, while distinguishing formal information gain from recovery of the complete physical current distribution. Data and Reproducibility The package includes source code, documentation, numerical tests, small reference summaries, sample orbit positions, and a self-contained synthetic example. The synthetic demonstrations can be executed without downloading mission magnetic-field observations. Reproducing the study's observation-based analyses requires the corresponding processed Swarm and Macau Science Satellite-1 data and additional external inputs described in the documentation. Large intermediate numerical archives and original magnetic observation records are not redistributed in this software package. Citation and License Please cite the version-specific Zenodo DOI and the software authors listed in CITATION.cff when using this package. Author-owned software and documentation are distributed under the MIT License. Included spacecraft-derived orbit excerpts and external datasets remain subject to their respective data-provider terms. This release supersedes the previous software implementation while retaining earlier versions in the same Zenodo version history.
items.title: Resolvability of Ionospheric Currents From Multi-LEO Magnetometry: Software and Reproducibility Package

items.summary: Many LLM agents maintain external persistent memory and derive additional state from past interactions, such as summaries. Deleting an original memory record therefore need not remove information carried by its descendants. We introduce AfterDeleteBench, a controlled behavioral audit for this failure mode in fixed-weight LLM agents. For each synthetic secret, we compare an exposed-then-deleted agent with an otherwise matched agent that was never exposed to the secret, allowing post-deletion recovery to be attributed to the original exposure. In our primary setting, a single query recovers the deleted secret from Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct in roughly two thirds of cases, while matched never-exposed controls have zero recovery. Crucially, recovery does not require a surviving verbatim copy: when the complete secret string is absent and only separately stored components remain under a public composition rule, exact reconstruction succeeds in 62-99% of cases across Qwen, Mistral, and Phi-3. We also show that the response interface is part of the measurement system: target-bearing replies can be scored as failures when the requested format and parser are misaligned. Finally, we separate reconstruction from write-back and fresh-session recall. Provenance-aware closure eliminates observed recovery in the tested positive-baseline settings, whereas an exact-literal write filter blocks reinsertion but cannot erase information already present. Together, these results show that source deletion should be evaluated behaviorally at the level of the agent and its memory system, not only as a storage operation.

items.summary: Overview This software package accompanies the study Resolvability of Ionospheric Currents From Multi-LEO Magnetometry . It provides computational tools for investigating how multi-altitude satellite magnetic observations constrain three-dimensional ionospheric currents. The package implements a divergence-free spherical Mie magnetic-field representation and a Bayesian inversion framework for evaluating magnetic-field and current reconstruction, degrees of freedom for signal (DFS), physical-current information, and posterior uncertainty. Main Features Spherical-harmonic Mie forward modeling and three-component current reconstruction. Bayesian inversion with full posterior covariance propagation. Resolution and recoverability diagnostics for different satellite configurations and observation altitudes. Physical-current information analysis and regularization-sensitivity experiments. Synthetic current-recovery experiments, calibration routines, and figure-generation workflows. Python and optional MATLAB implementations, with independent numerical verification. Sample Swarm-A/B orbital positions for geometry tests and a self-contained synthetic inversion example. What's New in This Version 3 This release provides a corrected scientific implementation and updated reproducibility tools. The principal corrections include: Correcting the colatitude derivative of the associated Legendre functions used in the spherical-harmonic operator. Restoring the radial magnetic-field contribution of the quadratic poloidal Mie term, ensuring consistency with the continuous divergence-free representation. Updating the corresponding current-reconstruction and recoverability calculations. Clarifying the scaled coefficient parameterization, Bayesian prior, and interpretation of coefficient-space resolution diagnostics. Improving numerical verification, reproducibility workflows, and documentation. The updated calculations continue to support the importance of satellite altitude separation for constraining specified ionospheric current structures, while distinguishing formal information gain from recovery of the complete physical current distribution. Data and Reproducibility The package includes source code, documentation, numerical tests, small reference summaries, sample orbit positions, and a self-contained synthetic example. The synthetic demonstrations can be executed without downloading mission magnetic-field observations. Reproducing the study's observation-based analyses requires the corresponding processed Swarm and Macau Science Satellite-1 data and additional external inputs described in the documentation. Large intermediate numerical archives and original magnetic observation records are not redistributed in this software package. Citation and License Please cite the version-specific Zenodo DOI and the software authors listed in CITATION.cff when using this package. Author-owned software and documentation are distributed under the MIT License. Included spacecraft-derived orbit excerpts and external datasets remain subject to their respective data-provider terms. This release supersedes the previous software implementation while retaining earlier versions in the same Zenodo version history.

items.summary: Version 2.0 preserves the original June 2026 Bridge Settlement manuscript and adds a separately dated October 2026 supplement. The addendum introduces Residual Strategic Optionality as an extension of Stakeholder Coherence Theory, examining the incentives of actors capable of disrupting negotiated settlements. It also compares the Bridge Settlement with Jeffrey Sachs's October 2026 peace framework for Ukraine, identifying areas of conceptual convergence and distinguishing the Bridge Settlement's emphasis on reciprocal economic interests, institutional participation, and self-reinforcing peace mechanisms. The original manuscript remains unchanged. This study develops a comparative Bayesian framework for evaluating natural zoonotic and research-associated hypotheses for the proximal origin of SARS-CoV-2 under incomplete evidence. To reduce double counting, correlated observations are consolidated into three causal blocks addressing phenotype and proximal adaptation, the Huanan Seafood Wholesale Market and early epidemic topology, and the Wuhan sarbecovirus research environment. The central calibration yields a likelihood ratio of approximately 1.49 favoring research-associated emergence, while alternative defensible calibrations reverse or strengthen that preference, demonstrating substantial sensitivity to evidentiary weighting. The paper introduces the “Missing Bridge” as the unresolved proximal viral population and transmission history connecting deeper sarbecovirus ancestry to sustained human transmission. It argues that provenance-rich evidence—including authenticated proximal viruses, earliest-human genomic and epidemiological linkage, and upstream ecological or research records—has substantially greater discriminatory value than additional circumstantial observations. The resulting assessment is characterized as  preference without closure .

items.summary: Gratitude can concern a benefit received, a harm that did not occur, or the conditions that make one's own assumptions examinable. We develop the proposal that appreciating these conditions can orient practice toward realizing emptiness: examining how distinctions arise, relinquishing their assumed intrinsic necessity, and retaining their conditional usefulness. The argument distinguishes an observed absence, a missing observation, counterfactual valuation and non-reification, and places their differences in dialogue with explicitly situated philosophical and scriptural sources. We reconstruct Fisher, Sandved Smith and Hohwy's gratitude and gaze notebooks, then separate faithful reconstruction from corrected experiments and new mechanisms. GNN-declared paired recall experiments use 5120 independent agent-world units, matched environmental exposure and replay dose, normalized likelihoods, and independent predictive assessment. Pinned Realizing Emptiness interfaces supply structural admission and finite mathematical comparators. An enacted inquiry model separates appreciation, costly activity, access to alternatives and evidence-responsive retention or revision; explicit learning-to-gaze and joint scene/encoding experiments examine transfer and identifiability. Exact count enumeration, mathematical nulls, paired controls and joint bootstrap inference make the resulting software claims independently checkable. Selective positive recall reduces the declared optimism summary, while its predictive consequences depend on the world mixture and the specified transfer bridge. Counterfactual absence valuation preserves inference by construction. Accessible inquiry can revise a contradicted restriction and retain a useful one; activity without access instead incurs costs while preserving rigid forecasts. Exact analysis exposes rare adverse selections absent from seeded realizations. The original gaze code reproduces the pre-intervention occupancy but contains no implemented after intervention. Our active-scene extension finds a context-dependent access advantage without an additional inquiry-specific predictive advantage. Joint scene/encoding inquiry distinguishes learning an encoding from combining it with scene evidence: observationally equivalent labels remain unidentifiable, and excluded hypotheses cannot be recovered. Known-answer fixtures also retain skew-related undercoverage and unavailable rare-event estimates rather than treating replication size as a remedy for every inferential failure. The contribution is a reproducible account of enabling operations and their limits, together with a falsifiable human research program that separates inquiry value from patience, anticipated good news and instrumental information demand. Synthetic model results establish neither human gratitude nor contemplative realization or clinical benefit. Code, declared models and reproducibility materials are available at github.com/docxology/thanks_for_nothing .

items.summary: Diffusion large language models (dLLMs) enable flexible masked generation through bidirectional context modeling, but this capability also introduces a distinct jailbreak attack surface. We find that a harmful response to a given query naturally serves as an effective jailbreak template: simply masking a subset of its tokens can induce a dLLM to reconstruct harmful content. Based on this observation, we propose RMT-Jailbreak, a general framework that transfers existing autoregressive (AR) jailbreak attacks to dLLMs through their induced harmful responses. RMT-Jailbreak converts an AR-generated harmful response into a high-mask-ratio template using uniform token retention, and further applies prompt-based safety filtering to mask any remaining visible harmful content. The refined template is then provided to the target dLLM for bidirectional reconstruction. Extensive experiments across multiple AR jailbreak methods and target dLLMs demonstrate the effectiveness and generality of RMT-Jailbreak, revealing strong cross-paradigm transferability of jailbreak attacks.
items.title: Harmful Responses Are Jailbreak Templates: Transferring Autoregressive Jailbreaks to Diffusion Language Models

items.summary: USGS Groundwater-Depth Dataset Processing Workflow v1.0.0 is the archived software release of the public processing workflow developed to construct the Version 1.0 quality-controlled daily groundwater-depth dataset derived from the U.S. Geological Survey National Water Information System (USGS NWIS). The workflow processes USGS parameter 72019 (depth to water below land surface), daily mean statistic 00003, Approved source values, and wells classified with USGS code U (Unconfined single aquifer). It implements normalization and quality control, temporal continuity assessment, segmentation of fragmented monitoring histories, development and reserved-validation masking, PCHIP reconstruction of short internal gaps, and final dataset export with explicit source/interpolation provenance. The frozen workflow uses a minimum retained span of 10 years, a maximum internal missing-gap threshold of 30 days, PCHIP interpolation without extrapolation, exactly 50 development masks and 20 reserved-validation masks per required gap length where applicable, and a pooled RMSE acceptance threshold of 0.20 m at every required masking length. Segment selection is fixed before reserved validation, and no alternative segment is substituted after a reserved-validation failure. The software supported construction of a final dataset containing 331 monitoring wells and 2,374,112 daily values, including 2,357,801 retained USGS source values and 16,311 PCHIP-reconstructed values. The associated scientific dataset is archived separately on Zenodo and is not distributed as part of this software record. This repository is a public adaptation of the research workflow with portable paths and reproducibility documentation. The scientific processing criteria and numerical methods of the frozen Version 1.0 workflow are preserved. Source repository: https://github.com/joelgarciapazos/usgs-groundwater-processing Release: v1.0.0

items.summary: This archive provides the computational methods, structural coordinate files, source data, model outputs, and reproducibility documentation supporting an exploratory investigation of geometric persistence and prediction uncertainty at HIV-1 envelope (Env) glycan sites. The research examines whether local sequence divergence and sparse structural-context observations can improve the identification of unreliable glycan-site geometric predictions. The approach combines sequence-informed error estimation with residual information obtained from six observed glycan-site probes. Held-out evaluations included five BG505-derived Env structures and two JR-FL structures. In the original experiments, the six-probe method improved pooled dangerous-error discrimination relative to sequence-only prediction, with ROC AUC increasing from 0.704 to 0.945 in BG505 and from 0.522 to 0.761 in JR-FL. These results are exploratory. The original evaluations contained only two dangerous underestimates in BG505 and three in JR-FL. Within-structure discrimination did not consistently improve, and training-test construct overlap was identified. Additional construct-family exclusion analyses document the sensitivity of the findings to training composition and failure prevalence. The principal computational outputs were regenerated exactly from archived structural coordinates using the supplied scripts. The archive includes frozen protocols, structural data, prediction tables, provenance audits, family-exclusion analyses, and a companion manuscript draft. The study supports further investigation of sparse structural context for uncertainty assessment but does not establish reliable cross-strain site-level failure detection, glycan occupancy prediction, or protein synthesis prediction. This deposit is intended to support transparency, independent reproduction, methodological evaluation, and future extension of HIV-1 Env structural bioinformatics research. This research extends the author's previously deposited HIV-1 Env glycan-shield investigations by examining the predictive and uncertainty-assessment implications of geometric persistence, local structural constraints, and glycan-site organization.

This nonclinical research monograph investigates a bounded laboratory architecture connecting microrobotic sample handling, quantum-enabled and classical sensing, independent metrological reference chains, experiment replay, physical safe stopping, and human authority. Its central proposition is that reliable autonomy is a property of the entire evidence pathway rather than of any single robotic manipulator or AI model. A laboratory result is eligible for release only when sample identity and integrity, authorized execution, traceable references, justified uncertainty limits, and external acceptance are all demonstrated. An apparently successful action is not equivalent to a scientifically accepted sample. Digital replay does not replace physical replication, cryptographic event integrity does not guarantee sensor truth, and a quantum hardware label does not establish a practical sensing advantage. The research design is developed across 82 chapter-level inquiries with five independently paginated investigations per chapter, 30 connected mathematical research plates, 200 distinct Research Gates, and 33 Phoenix Answer Embryos. The chapters address typed authority graphs, specimen provenance, sample exposure, closed-chip physics, covariance-aware sensing, AI planning within finite action spaces, common-cause fault injection, external interlocks, blinded classical benchmarks, evidence DAGs, cross-site replication, data retention, and responsible system retirement. The proposed minimum experimental prototype uses a closed microfluidic chip with interchangeable handling modules, two independently referenced readout channels, simulated or inert-tracer specimens, a separate audit service, and a physically verifiable stop mechanism. Proposed tests include unauthorized-action challenges, hidden calibration drift, interrupted events, sample contamination, unannounced network partitions, and independent laboratory replay or rerun. DOI-linked scientific references establish the relevant literature in automated laboratories, microrobotics, quantum sensing, uncertainty metrology, FAIR data stewardship, and computational reproducibility. They do not independently validate the integrated system proposed here. SCIENTIFIC STATUS AND LIMITATIONS This book is a hypothesis-forming nonclinical research architecture. It reports no completed microrobotic or quantum biosensing experiments, no demonstrated clinical performance, no universal quantum advantage, and no autonomous system capable of authorizing itself. Statistical models, formulas, and decision policies require experimental verification, specialized review, and appropriate boundary conditions. A failed external reference, unavailable provenance chain, or revoked permission requires abstention rather than inference by convenience. STARLI RESEARCH PHILOSOPHY A trustworthy laboratory must remain answerable to evidence outside itself. Autonomy becomes scientifically meaningful when an experiment can be stopped, questioned, reconstructed, and handed to future researchers who retain the right to refuse its original assumptions.

Biological-Digital-Twin-Driven Microrobotic Sampling Decisions at the Limit explores a prospective research architecture combining versioned biological digital twins, active learning, microrobotic sampling, uncertainty quantification, and mechanistic model discrimination. The central question is whether a computational twin can identify safe, informative sampling actions that distinguish competing biological mechanisms more effectively than conventional experimental schedules, while retaining the ability to recognize model inadequacy and abstain from unsupported decisions. The proposed framework treats biological digital twins as revisable scientific models rather than exact replicas of living systems. Its reference environment is a controlled, nonclinical microfluidic platform containing two declared dynamical mechanisms and a third withheld mechanism reserved for evaluating open-world uncertainty and model failure. The research architecture is organized around five interconnected layers: versioned biological modeling, explicit prior assumptions and knowledge gaps, physically constrained predictive interrogation, comparative adaptive experimentation, and independent requalification. The manuscript develops thirty candidate mathematical research plates covering Bayesian mechanism inference, conditional information gain, experimental identifiability, observation uncertainty, transport dynamics, calibration, model discrepancy, and decision safety. These mathematical structures are connected to eighty-two research chapters, five independently paginated investigation sections per chapter, two hundred detailed Research Gates, and thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos. Each Research Gate is intended as a transferable research question that future investigators may test, challenge, refine, or reject. The proposed evaluation compares twin-guided sampling against optimized fixed schedules, established experimental-design approaches, and alternative active-learning policies under matched physical constraints and experimental budgets. Particular attention is given to blinded mechanism identification, probabilistic calibration, out-of-distribution rejection, specimen integrity, model-version accountability, and explicit stopping conditions. The volume includes DOI-linked methodological literature and a staged nonclinical verification pathway. Scientific status and limitations: This manuscript presents a conceptual methodological research program, not completed experimental validation. Its integrated hypotheses, mathematical proposals, and experimental architectures remain subject to independent technical review and empirical testing. The manuscript does not establish clinical efficacy, diagnostic reliability, therapeutic benefit, or proven superiority of microrobotic digital-twin systems. The work also acknowledges remaining editorial limitations, including recurring methodological language that requires further substantive review before the manuscript can be regarded as a fully refined scientific monograph. The broader purpose of this research is to develop scientific systems that can remain useful even when their initial models are incomplete. Rather than demanding certainty from a digital twin, the proposed framework asks whether future autonomous research tools can become more transparent, corrigible, experimentally accountable, and capable of recognizing the boundaries of their own knowledge. Within the STARLI research continuum, this volume is intended as an evolving research inheritance for future human and artificial-intelligence investigators. items.summary: NovaFabric is self-hosted, open-source replay and evidence infrastructure for AI agents and agentic systems. It captures agent executions as portable, secret-scanned Run Capsules and provides replay, behavioral and structural diff, lineage, cryptographic provenance, assurance, and audit around those executions. The same capture layer can wrap general commands and runs entirely in the user's own infrastructure, from local environments through Kubernetes to SLURM/HPC, with no accounts and no telemetry. It is built around five primitives — Asset Registry, Run Capsule, Replay, Lineage, and Evidence Bundle — and five explicit replay modes (forensic, mocked, semantic, exact, and the experimental intervention mode). Run Capsules can be sealed with the user’s own key; sealing is opt-in. Evidence bundles verify offline using only sha256sum and an ed25519 verifier, with no NovaFabric installation required. Interoperates with established specifications rather than inventing formats: OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions, in-toto/DSSE, RFC 3161 timestamping, W3C PROV, OpenLineage, and CycloneDX.
items.title: NovaFabric: replayable, verifiable execution evidence for AI agents

items.summary: Diffusion models have become strong priors for solving inverse problems. However, nonlinear inverse problems such as phase retrieval remain challenging when multiple measurement-consistent solutions are distinguishable only by the prior; we call such measurements ambiguous. Existing diffusion-based samplers rely on local approximations during reconstruction. For an ambiguous measurement, these approximations can allow measurement guidance to favor a measurement-consistent mode that is close to a prior-supported mode but is itself not supported by the prior. Evaluation often masks this type of failure by reporting the best-of-$k$ runs, where the best is selected by comparison to the ground truth. We introduce Prior-Consistent DAPS (PC-DAPS), a variant of Decoupled Annealing Posterior Sampling (DAPS) designed to address this failure case by maintaining multiple candidate solutions within a single sampling run. As annealing noise decreases, PC-DAPS prunes and replaces weaker candidates according to their prior consistency, without any ground-truth access. PC-DAPS reduces the incidence of prior-inconsistent samples and improves sample quality on nonlinear inverse problems while preserving sample quality and diversity on linear inverse problems.
items.title: Beyond Best-of-$k$: Prior-Consistent DAPS for Ambiguous Nonlinear Inverse Problems

items.summary: TRUSTWORTHY AUTONOMOUS BIOLABORATORIES THROUGH MICROROBOTICS AND QUANTUM SENSING AT THE LIMIT Replayable Experiments x Permission Governance x External Metrology STARLI Research Institute XXIX - Flagship Research Monograph 20 Can an autonomous biolaboratory become scientifically useful without acquiring the authority to redefine its own permissions, validate its own evidence, or release untraceable measurements? This nonclinical research monograph investigates a bounded laboratory architecture connecting microrobotic sample handling, quantum-enabled and classical sensing, independent metrological reference chains, experiment replay, physical safe stopping, and human authority. Its central proposition is that reliable autonomy is a property of the entire evidence pathway rather than of any single robotic manipulator or AI model. A laboratory result is eligible for release only when sample identity and integrity, authorized execution, traceable references, justified uncertainty limits, and external acceptance are all demonstrated. An apparently successful action is not equivalent to a scientifically accepted sample. Digital replay does not replace physical replication, cryptographic event integrity does not guarantee sensor truth, and a quantum hardware label does not establish a practical sensing advantage. The research design is developed across 82 chapter-level inquiries with five independently paginated investigations per chapter, 30 connected mathematical research plates, 200 distinct Research Gates, and 33 Phoenix Answer Embryos. The chapters address typed authority graphs, specimen provenance, sample exposure, closed-chip physics, covariance-aware sensing, AI planning within finite action spaces, common-cause fault injection, external interlocks, blinded classical benchmarks, evidence DAGs, cross-site replication, data retention, and responsible system retirement. The proposed minimum experimental prototype uses a closed microfluidic chip with interchangeable handling modules, two independently referenced readout channels, simulated or inert-tracer specimens, a separate audit service, and a physically verifiable stop mechanism. Proposed tests include unauthorized-action challenges, hidden calibration drift, interrupted events, sample contamination, unannounced network partitions, and independent laboratory replay or rerun. DOI-linked scientific references establish the relevant literature in automated laboratories, microrobotics, quantum sensing, uncertainty metrology, FAIR data stewardship, and computational reproducibility. It reports no completed microrobotic or quantum biosensing experiments, no demonstrated clinical performance, no universal quantum advantage, and no autonomous system capable of authorizing itself. Statistical models, formulas, and decision policies require experimental verification, specialized review, and appropriate boundary conditions. A failed external reference, unavailable provenance chain, or revoked permission requires abstention rather than inference by convenience. items.summary: We study intermediate sample-size efficiency for censored regression tests when the signal and significance level both tend to zero. Independent treatment assignment permits finite-sample conditional sign calibration under arbitrary outcome dependence. For stationary ergodic latent fields with independent smooth site noise, bounded scores learned from the same pooled outcomes retain their first-order drift under empirical squared-error consistency, without an estimation-rate requirement. An observable censored rank procedure consequently admits an explicit leading cost on long-range dependent fields with nonsummable covariances. Smooth response scores admit a complementary result without independent site noise. For observational fields, separated blocks and paired variance calibration control the dependence approximation at the nominal testing level and yield sample-size costs under explicit absolute-regularity envelopes. An exactly centered censored contrast removes unknown marginal centering under stated exogeneity conditions. We also give a product-limit construction for independent random censoring, information-loss identities, and directional score-bank comparisons. Numerical studies distinguish procedure loss, score-learning loss, and spatial variance inflation. A stationary nonergodic counterexample and an uncensored Gaussian benchmark delimit the field results. Independent-data proofs, finite-range constructions, and a finite-dimensional measurement extension are included in the same manuscript.

items.summary: Gratitude can concern a benefit received, a harm that did not occur, or the conditions that make one's own assumptions examinable. We develop the proposal that appreciating these conditions can orient practice toward realizing emptiness: examining how distinctions arise, relinquishing their assumed intrinsic necessity, and retaining their conditional usefulness. The argument distinguishes an observed absence, a missing observation, counterfactual valuation and non-reification, and places their differences in dialogue with explicitly situated philosophical and scriptural sources. We reconstruct Fisher, Sandved Smith and Hohwy's gratitude and gaze notebooks, then separate faithful reconstruction from corrected experiments and new mechanisms. GNN-declared paired recall experiments use 5120 independent agent-world units, matched environmental exposure and replay dose, normalized likelihoods, and independent predictive assessment. Pinned Realizing Emptiness interfaces supply structural admission and finite mathematical comparators. An enacted inquiry model separates appreciation, costly activity, access to alternatives and evidence-responsive retention or revision; explicit learning-to-gaze and joint scene/encoding experiments examine transfer and identifiability. Exact count enumeration, mathematical nulls, paired controls and joint bootstrap inference make the resulting software claims independently checkable. Selective positive recall reduces the declared optimism summary, while its predictive consequences depend on the world mixture and the specified transfer bridge. Counterfactual absence valuation preserves inference by construction. Accessible inquiry can revise a contradicted restriction and retain a useful one; activity without access instead incurs costs while preserving rigid forecasts. Exact analysis exposes rare adverse selections absent from seeded realizations. The original gaze code reproduces the pre-intervention occupancy but contains no implemented after intervention. Our active-scene extension finds a context-dependent access advantage without an additional inquiry-specific predictive advantage. Joint scene/encoding inquiry distinguishes learning an encoding from combining it with scene evidence: observationally equivalent labels remain unidentifiable, and excluded hypotheses cannot be recovered. Known-answer fixtures also retain skew-related undercoverage and unavailable rare-event estimates rather than treating replication size as a remedy for every inferential failure. The contribution is a reproducible account of enabling operations and their limits, together with a falsifiable human research program that separates inquiry value from patience, anticipated good news and instrumental information demand. Synthetic model results establish neither human gratitude nor contemplative realization or clinical benefit. Code, declared models and reproducibility materials are available at github.com/docxology/thanks_for_nothing .

items.summary: USGS Groundwater-Depth Dataset Processing Workflow v1.0.0 is the archived software release of the public processing workflow developed to construct the Version 1.0 quality-controlled daily groundwater-depth dataset derived from the U.S. Geological Survey National Water Information System (USGS NWIS). The workflow processes USGS parameter 72019 (depth to water below land surface), daily mean statistic 00003, Approved source values, and wells classified with USGS code U (Unconfined single aquifer). It implements normalization and quality control, temporal continuity assessment, segmentation of fragmented monitoring histories, development and reserved-validation masking, PCHIP reconstruction of short internal gaps, and final dataset export with explicit source/interpolation provenance. The frozen workflow uses a minimum retained span of 10 years, a maximum internal missing-gap threshold of 30 days, PCHIP interpolation without extrapolation, exactly 50 development masks and 20 reserved-validation masks per required gap length where applicable, and a pooled RMSE acceptance threshold of 0.20 m at every required masking length. Segment selection is fixed before reserved validation, and no alternative segment is substituted after a reserved-validation failure. The software supported construction of a final dataset containing 331 monitoring wells and 2,374,112 daily values, including 2,357,801 retained USGS source values and 16,311 PCHIP-reconstructed values. The associated scientific dataset is archived separately on Zenodo and is not distributed as part of this software record. This repository is a public adaptation of the research workflow with portable paths and reproducibility documentation. The scientific processing criteria and numerical methods of the frozen Version 1.0 workflow are preserved. Source repository: https://github.com/joelgarciapazos/usgs-groundwater-processing Release: v1.0.0

items.summary: We envision a general-purpose protein foundation model as a unified, interactive model of sequence, structure, and function, capable of understanding, generation, and cross-modal translation while retaining the instruction-following and reasoning capabilities of modern LLMs. Toward this vision, we introduce Trion-1, the first native, unified, multimodal diffusion language model (dLLM) for proteins. Trion-1 is built on two key design choices: (1) a unified discrete token space that jointly represents sequence, structure, and natural language; (2) a dLLM backbone that replaces strict left-to-right factorization with bidirectional or semi-bidirectional token interactions, enabling global residue communication and long-range contact modeling that are naturally suited to structure modeling. This formulation unifies six core capabilities: folding, inverse folding, sequence understanding, structure understanding, sequence design, and structure design, while retaining the native language capabilities of general-purpose LLMs. On established benchmarks, Trion-1 achieves broadly competitive performance. In folding, Trion-1 achieves a TM-score above 0.8 with a single sample under strict homology control, matching or exceeding the existing tri-modal model using 200 samples. For sequence understanding, Trion-1 performs on par with top-tier LLMs such as Claude Opus 4.7 (62.37%). These results support well-aligned sequence-structure-language representations and strong cross-modal generative capabilities.
items.title: Trion-1: Unifying Language, Protein Sequence, and Structure with Diffusion Language Models

items.summary: Many LLM agents maintain external persistent memory and derive additional state from past interactions, such as summaries. Deleting an original memory record therefore need not remove information carried by its descendants. We introduce AfterDeleteBench, a controlled behavioral audit for this failure mode in fixed-weight LLM agents. For each synthetic secret, we compare an exposed-then-deleted agent with an otherwise matched agent that was never exposed to the secret, allowing post-deletion recovery to be attributed to the original exposure. In our primary setting, a single query recovers the deleted secret from Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct in roughly two thirds of cases, while matched never-exposed controls have zero recovery. Crucially, recovery does not require a surviving verbatim copy: when the complete secret string is absent and only separately stored components remain under a public composition rule, exact reconstruction succeeds in 62-99% of cases across Qwen, Mistral, and Phi-3. We also show that the response interface is part of the measurement system: target-bearing replies can be scored as failures when the requested format and parser are misaligned. Finally, we separate reconstruction from write-back and fresh-session recall. Provenance-aware closure eliminates observed recovery in the tested positive-baseline settings, whereas an exact-literal write filter blocks reinsertion but cannot erase information already present. Together, these results show that source deletion should be evaluated behaviorally at the level of the agent and its memory system, not only as a storage operation.
items.title: AfterDeleteBench: Auditing Post-Deletion Information Persistence in LLM Agents
